title: Dedicated autoscaler failing to provision burst capacity leading to reserved-pool shortfalls for customers
text:
Dedicated autoscaler failing to provision burst capacity leading to reserved-pool shortfalls for customers

description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported tail latency spikes and request failures between 2026-03-12T22:10Z and 2026-03-13T03:40Z. Symptoms: queued requests for Dedicated reserved pools did not trigger expected burst allocations; new requests received 503s or long queue times despite available total cluster capacity. Affected tenants were on reserved pools with configured burst limits. This ticket tracks the live incident, triage, short-term mitigations, root cause analysis, fix rollout, and follow-ups.

updates:
2026-03-13 22:45 UTC - PagerDuty triggered. On-call rotation: Liam O'Connor alerted. Initial triage shows reservePoolManager reported capacityAvailable=false while node capacity metrics show GPUs idle in other pools.
2026-03-13 23:15 UTC - Scoped impact to 3 dedicated customers (legal-tech-prod, commerce-ml, fintech-sim) all with similar reservedPool configs (min=8, burst=12). CS sent proactive notices; SRE began manual capacity bump attempt.
2026-03-13 23:50 UTC - Hotfix deployed: rolled back autoscaler microservice from v2.14.0 -> v2.13.4 in us-west-2 canary. Canary behaved normally. Manual increase of burst_limit accepted for two customers as emergency measure.
2026-03-14 01:30 UTC - Root-cause hypothesis updated: recent change in allocator accounting (PR #4121) introduced a race where ephemeral allocation marks were not cleared when burst evaluation aborted, resulting in undercounting free GPUs for the burst decision path.
2026-03-14 02:10 UTC - Engineering team confirmed repro locally with synthetic workload that triggers allocation abort path while concurrent preemption occurs. Created fix branch: fix/autoscaler-clear-alloc-marks.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC - Emergency PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4173. Runs include additional unit tests to exercise abort+preempt code path.
2026-03-14 11:20 UTC - Mitigation: applied conservative fallback on scale decision so that aborted allocations are treated as available for 30s. Observed decrease in 503s for affected customers in us-west-2. Monitoring to run for 72h before full rollout.
2026-03-14 15:40 UTC - Customer follow-up: support case INC-2026-334 shipped status update; legal-tech-prod requested SLA credit evaluation. Customer success loop initiated.
2026-03-14 16:05 UTC - Plan: merge hotfix after green CI and canary for 6 hours, then progressive rollout across other regions. Postmortem timeline added to follow-ups.

investigation_summary:
Investigation combined autoscaler logs, allocator traces, and GPU occupancy metrics. We instrumented reservePoolManager and the allocator's ephemeralAllocation context to capture aborted allocation markers. Hypothesis validated: when an allocation attempt fails in the burst decision path (due to concurrent scheduling/preemptions), a flag 'alloc_marked' remained true and was not cleared, making capacity accounting treat that GPU as unavailable for subsequent burst decisions. This behavior began after rollout of PR #4121 which adjusted the abort flow for faster failure reporting but missed a cleanup path.

root_cause:
A race in the autoscaler/allocator abort flow introduced by PR #4121. The code path that aborts an allocation did not clear the ephemeral allocation marker in the case where the allocation failed before being committed. As a result, availableCapacity calculation used by burst gating considered these GPUs reserved and refused to provision additional burst nodes, causing shortfall even though physical GPUs were idle elsewhere in the cluster.

mitigation:
Short-term: rolled back autoscaler to v2.13.4 in the affected region; applied emergency policy to accept manual burst_limit increases and implemented a 30s cleanup grace where aborted allocs are returned to pool. Medium-term: merged PR fix to ensure cleanup in all abort/exception paths and added telemetry. Long-term: add stronger invariants in allocator (ownership token + TTL), comprehensive unit/integration test for abort scenarios, and an alert if logical free GPUs diverge from physical free GPUs by >5%.

postmortem_followups:
Add unit tests covering abort path (ENG-5941-FU1)
Extend integration test harness to simulate concurrent preemption and allocation aborts (ENG-5941-FU2)
Audit PR #4121 for other missing cleanup paths and harden code review checklist for allocator changes (ENG-5941-FU3)
Create dashboard showing physical vs logical available GPUs with 1m resolution and set alert (pager) when mismatch >5% (ENG-5941-FU4)
Customer remediation: prepare SLA credit playbook and coordinate with Customer Success for affected customers (ENG-5941-FU5)

tests_and_validation:
Unit: added tests for ephemeral allocation cleanup in abort and exception handlers
Integration: harness simulating 2000 concurrent requests across 5 tenants with reserved pools and burst thresholds, validating no 503s when physical capacity exists
Canary: successful canary in us-west-2 for 6 hours with no increase in errors before wider rollout
Perf: measured latency and allocation decision time to avoid regressions (<5ms added to decision time)
Chaos: schedule preemption during canary to validate cleanup under realistic flapping

notes:
Do not re-enable autoscaler v2.14.0 until fix merged and 24h post-canary is green
This incident highlights the risk of small allocator changes affecting business-critical reserved pool guarantees; prioritize additional code review for similar components
Consider redesigning burst gating to use lease tokens with TTL to avoid stale markers
